idea: An app that helps independent restaurants track food inventory to reduce waste

problem.problem_statement: Independent restaurants lose money on spoiled inventory and over-ordering because they still track stock with paper lists and spreadsheets.
existing_solutions: Paper clipboards and weekly walk-in counts
demand_signals: Restaurant owners discuss waste on operator forums
Incumbent reviews complain that inventory tools are too complex

customers.name: Independent restaurants with 1-3 locations
pain_points: Managers lack time for complex inventory software
customers.size_estimate: Hundreds of thousands of independent US restaurants

competitors.name: MarketMan
competitors.description: Restaurant inventory and purchasing platform used by multi-location operators.
weaknesses: Too heavy for a single independent cafe

competitors.name: BlueCart
competitors.description: Ordering and inventory for foodservice businesses.
weaknesses: Broader suite than a waste-first tool

economics.market_size: US restaurant inventory / back-office software is a multi-hundred-million-dollar category.
economics.revenue_potential: Realistic independent-restaurant pricing sits near $49–$99/month, not $300+ enterprise suites.

business_models.reasoning: Matches SMB restaurant software willingness to pay and undercuts heavy incumbents.

economics.unit_economics: Viable only if onboarding stays product-led; high-touch sales would erase SMB margins.

evidence.content: Independent restaurants routinely cite food waste as a margin problem and still use clipboards or spreadsheets.
The pain is high severity for independent restaurants with 1-3 locations because spoilage hits already-thin food costs.
MarketMan charges roughly $99–$249/month and targets operators who need full inventory and purchasing.
Users complain that existing inventory suites are too complex for a single independent restaurant.
There is a gap for a waste-first, lightweight tool, but the broader inventory category is crowded with incumbents.
Realistic pricing for independents is $49–$99/month; a $300 suite is unlikely to sell to this buyer.
We assume owners will adopt an iPad app without changing kitchen habits.
Average customer acquisition cost for independent restaurants in this category is unknown.

unknowns.question: What is a realistic CAC for independent restaurant software sold product-led?
unknowns.hypothesis: If CAC exceeds ~3 months of subscription, SMB unit economics break.

unknowns.question: Will line cooks actually log waste daily without manager enforcement?
unknowns.hypothesis: Adoption fails unless logging is automatic or takes under 30 seconds.

research_history.findings_summary: Confirmed waste pain for independents; current workaround is spreadsheets.
MarketMan and BlueCart exist; complexity complaints create a wedge.
SMB pricing works only with low-touch onboarding.
